paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Pride is a dangerous thing to carry, and Belshazzar carried it into a party. Daniel tells him he knew what happened to his father Nebuchadnezzar, who was brought low until he acknowledged that the Most High God rules over the kingdom of mankind (Daniel 5:21-22). Belshazzar knew the lesson and still didn't humble his heart. Knowing the right thing and doing it are two different batches, baker.

Look at what Belshazzar put his praise on. Daniel says they were gods "which cannot see or hear or understand," while the true God is the One "who holds in His hand your very breath and all your ways" (Daniel 5:23). Think about that. The king was breathing on God's loan the whole time and thanking a rolling pin. Everything we have comes from God's hand, so the thanks belong to Him.

Notice Daniel, too. He turned down the purple and the gold chain, and he still told the king the truth (Daniel 5:17). I think that's what it looks like when your eyes are on God and not on the prize. Daniel also tells Belshazzar that God had sent the hand, so the king's days were in God's hands, not his own (Daniel 5:24-26). So stay humble, give God the glory, and listen while there's still time, baker.
